data.narrative:
Radiant, a Series D nuclear energy company founded by Doug Bernauer, has raised $465M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 sector peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and yields a $1.5B result. This approach applies a standard 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier to Radiant's $1.0B last post-money valuation. The Peer-Median method is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer comparables; while six same-sector peers exist, none meet narrow stage/tier filters simultaneously (minimum three datapoints required), and using an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable cross-sector bias.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B–$1.7B, with a median of $1.5B. This range reflects conservative bounds around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage/similar-tier public or private nuclear energy comparables, which limits cross-validation. The median estimate relies entirely on stage-progression mechanics rather than market multiples, introducing model risk if Radiant's capital efficiency or technology risk profile diverges materially from typical Series D step-up assumptions. Additional uncertainty stems from nascent nuclear energy market pricing and regulatory timeline risk, neither of which are quantified in available peer data.
